text: Two matrices A and A′ are similar, i.e. A′ = P⁻¹AP for some invertible P. The best interpretation is:
choices: They represent the same linear operator with respect to two different bases
They have the same kernel as subspaces of Fⁿ
They differ only by a permutation of rows
explanation: If P is the change-of-basis matrix, then [T] in the new basis is P⁻¹[T]P. Consequently similarity preserves every basis-independent invariant — rank, determinant, trace, characteristic polynomial — though the kernel as a concrete subspace moves to P⁻¹(ker A).
